lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا إِدريس. أَعيشُ هُنا وَحدي مُنذُ سَنَوات
lines.english: I am Idris. I have lived here alone for years.
lines.transliteration: ana idriis. a'iishu hunaa wahdii mundhu sanawaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَبَلُ مُعَلِّمي وَصَديقي
lines.english: The mountain is my teacher and my friend.
lines.transliteration: al-jabalu mu'allimii wa sadiiqii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَبَلُ يَعلَم... ماذا تَبحَث عَنه؟
lines.english: The mountain knows... what do you seek?
lines.transliteration: al-jabalu ya'lam... maadha tabhath 'anhu?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطَّبيعَةُ لُغَة بِلا كَلِمات. لَكِن نَحتاج كَلِمات أَيضاً
lines.english: Nature is a language without words. But we need words too.
lines.transliteration: at-tabii'atu lugha bilaa kalimaat. laakin nahtaaj kalimaat aydan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَمْل — الصَّحراء تَتَكَلَّم بِالرَّمل
lines.english: Sand — the desert speaks with sand.
lines.transliteration: raml — as-sahraa' tatakallam bir-raml

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَجَرَة — الصَّبر كَالشَّجَرَة، يَنمو بِبُطء
lines.english: Tree — patience is like a tree, it grows slowly.
lines.transliteration: shajara — as-sabr kash-shajara, yanmuu bibu't'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَقولون أَنَّ في هَذا الجَبَل كَنزاً مَخفِيّاً
lines.english: They say there is a hidden treasure in this mountain.
lines.transliteration: yaquuluun anna fii haadha al-jabal kanzan makhfiyyan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِنَّ الكَنز الحَقيقي هُوَ المَعرِفَة
lines.english: But the real treasure is knowledge.
lines.transliteration: laakinna al-kanz al-haqiiqii huwa al-ma'rifa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَبَل يَختَبِر مَن يَدخُل
lines.english: The mountain tests those who enter.
lines.transliteration: al-jabal yakhtabir man yadkhul

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: إِذا عَرَفتَ الكَلِمات، سَتَجِد الطَّريق
lines.english: If you know the words, you will find the way.
lines.transliteration: idhaa 'arafta al-kalimaat, satajid at-tariiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ. الجَبَلُ لا يَنسى مَن طَلَبَ الحِكمَة
lines.english: You returned. The mountain never forgets those who sought wisdom.
lines.transliteration: 'udta. al-jabal laa yansaa man talaba al-hikma

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَبر — الصَّبرُ مِفتاحُ الفَرَج. كَلِمَة عَظيمَة
lines.english: Sabr — patience is the key to relief. A great word.
lines.transliteration: sabr — as-sabru miftaahu al-faraj. kalima 'aziima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَقَولُ المَثَل: "الصَّبرُ مِفتاحُ الفَرَج" — بِالعَرَبِيَّة يُصبِح شِعراً
lines.english: And the proverb: "Patience is the key to relief" — in Arabic it becomes poetry.
lines.transliteration: wa qawlu al-mathal: "as-sabru miftaahu al-faraj" — bil-arabiyya yusbih shi'ran
lines.culturalNote: Arabic proverbs (أَمثال, amthaal) are a cornerstone of classical learning. The proverb "الصَّبرُ مِفتاحُ الفَرَج" (patience is the key to relief) appears in Imam al-Ghazali's 12th-century Ihya Ulum al-Din.

choices.english: Wisdom lives here. Thank you, Idris.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَبَل يَرحَّب بِك مَرَّة أُخرى. لِنَتَأَمَّل
lines.english: The mountain welcomes you again. Let us reflect.
lines.transliteration: al-jabal yurahahib bik marra ukhraa. linata'ammal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حِكمَة — وَكَلِمَة "حَكيم" تَعني الحَكيم أَو الطَّبيب في العَرَبِيَّة القَديمَة
lines.english: Hikma — wisdom. And "hakim" means wise man or physician in classical Arabic.
lines.transliteration: hikma — wa kalima "hakiim" ta'nii al-hakiim aw at-tabiib fil-arabiyya al-qadiima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابن سينا لَقَّبوه "الشَّيخ الرَّئيس" — رَئيس الحُكَماء
lines.english: Ibn Sina was titled "al-Shaykh al-Ra'is" — Chief of the Wise.
lines.transliteration: ibn siinaa laqqabuuh "ash-shaykh ar-ra'iis" — ra'iis al-hukamaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَ"elixir" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن الكيمياء العَرَبِيَّة "الإِكسير"
lines.english: And English "elixir" came from Arabic alchemy: "al-iksir".
lines.transliteration: wa "elixir" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min al-kiimyaa' al-arabiyya "al-iksir"
lines.culturalNote: "Elixir" derives from Arabic al-iksir (الإِكسير), itself from Greek xerion. Arab alchemists like Jabir ibn Hayyan (8th c.) developed systematic chemistry — the word "alchemy" itself comes from Arabic al-kimiya (الكيمياء), from Coptic kemi (black earth/Egypt).

choices.arabic: العِلمُ العَرَبي في كُلّ مَكان! شُكراً إِدريس
choices.english: Arabic science is everywhere! Thank you, Idris.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكِتابَة العَرَبِيَّة تَسير مِن اليَمين إلى اليَسار — كَالشَّمس تَغرُب
lines.english: Arabic writing goes from right to left — like the sun setting.
lines.transliteration: al-kitaaba al-arabiyya tasiir min al-yamiin ilaa al-yasaar — kashams taghrub

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَذر "ك-ت-ب": كَتَبَ — يَكتُب — كِتاب — كاتِب — مَكتَبَة — مَكتَب
lines.english: Root K-T-B: kataba (he wrote) — yaktub (he writes) — kitaab (book) — kaatib (writer) — maktaba (library) — maktab (office).
lines.transliteration: jadhr k-t-b: kataba — yaktub — kitaab — kaatib — maktaba — maktab
lines.culturalNote: The Arabic trilateral root K-T-B (ك-ت-ب) demonstrates the system's power: from three letters, the language generates dozens of related words. Learning one root unlocks a whole vocabulary family — this is why Arabic learners say "once you see the roots, the language opens up."

choices.english: Roots open the world! Thank you, Idris.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِجلِس. خُذ نَفَساً. "تَفَكَّر" — العَقل يَحتاج الهُدوء
lines.english: Sit. Take a breath. "Tafakkar" — the mind needs quiet.
lines.transliteration: ijlis. khudh nafasan. "tafakkar" — al-'aql yahtaaj al-huduu'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَة "تَفَكَّر" تَعني التَّأَمُّل العَميق — فِكر عَميق
lines.english: "Tafakkar" means deep reflection — profound thought.
lines.transliteration: kalima "tafakkar" ta'nii at-ta'ammul al-'amiiq — fikr 'amiiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِن أَعلى الجَبَل أَرى الدُّنيا كَما رَآها لَبيد بنُ رَبيعَة
lines.english: From the mountain top I see the world as Labid ibn Rabi'ah saw it

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَفَتِ الدِّيارُ — هَل تَعرِفُ مُعَلَّقَة لَبيد؟ سَنَختَبِرُ ذَلِك الآن
lines.english: The abodes have faded — do you know Labid's Ode? We shall test that now
